clue.text: Returning prisoner changed shoes for protective footwear

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word for the convict is read right to left

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual convict

indicators.note: letters that are changed have been rearranged into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A convict back from prison swaps his shoes for sturdier boots.
explanation.walkthrough: GAL from LAG backwards, then OSHES from the jumbled shoes: GALOSHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to protect ordinary shoes from rain and mud.

clue.text: Mineral from isthmus pygmies sent north

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters north means reading them bottom to top
from says the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the tail of the first word and the head of the second

explanation.surface: Mineral ore found on a narrow land bridge is shipped up the map by small-statured people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, isthMUS PYGmies gives GYPSUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate mineral used to make plaster.

clue.text: One with no respect for environment butchered big turtle

definitions.text: One with no respect for environment

indicators.note: butchered means cut up and mangled, so the letters are hacked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eco-vandal slaughtered a large sea turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug drops rubbish in public places, showing disregard for the surroundings.

clue.text: Upstanding detective protecting easily-led female gets stitched up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom
protecting means guarding by surrounding, so the detective letters enclose the animal

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
a female sheep, sheep being proverbially easy to lead

explanation.surface: An honest detective shielding a gullible woman is framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' reads as honest and 'stitched up' as framed; both are double-edged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewed is the past tense of sew, to join with needle and thread, which is to stitch.

clue.text: Paradise Island? Yes, life is sorted!

indicators.note: sorted means arranged in a new order, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An island paradise where life is all sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Elysian Fields were the blessed afterlife home of heroes, a paradise.

clue.text: Smashes holes in sides of barrels

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stave in a door or hull is to break a hole in it
second meaning: the curved wooden strips that form a cask's sides

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a cooper's casks by bashing in their sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is used in the phrasal form 'stave in', which is why the definition keeps its 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for breaking inward and the plural noun for the timber strips a barrel is built from.

clue.text: Slender, toothless gizmo

parts.note: slender means thin
a toothless smile shows only gums

explanation.surface: A description of a skinny, toothless gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy is a placeholder name for an object whose name escapes you, much like gizmo.

clue.text: Central characters in novel about Colditz liked a drink

indicators.note: central characters are the middle letters of each of the words that follow

parts.note: middle letter
middle letter
middle letter
middle letter
a one-letter word is its own middle

explanation.surface: The main characters in a war novel set at Colditz enjoyed a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central characters' reads as the heroes of the book; it means the middle letters. Colditz was a German castle used as a WW2 prison camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear distilled spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Condemn structure in speech

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a judge passes a penalty on a convict
second meaning: a grammatical unit of words

explanation.surface: Criticise the way a speech is put together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for a court imposing punishment and a noun for a complete grammatical unit of language.

clue.text: Tracks run out from separate holding centre in Wolverhampton

indicators.note: holding means the shortened phrase wraps around another letter
the centre of the city name is the single letter at its exact middle
run out from says the cricket abbreviation for a run is driven out of the phrase for separate

parts.note: to part ways is to separate
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
the seventh of its thirteen letters sits in the middle

explanation.surface: Footpaths leading out of a split-off hub somewhere in Wolverhampton, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from PARTWAYS to get PATWAYS, then put the middle letter of Wolverhampton inside: PATHWAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathways and tracks are both narrow routes made for walking across country.

clue.text: Outgoing leader rings daughter as instructed

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the name goes around the other letter

parts.note: Joe Biden, the US president at the end of his term when the puzzle ran
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A departing head of state phones his daughter, as he was told to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' reads as telephoning, but it means surrounding: BI(D)DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidden is the past participle of bid, to command, so something bidden has been instructed.

clue.text: Infection consuming upper-class womaniser

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the infection letters go around the class letter

parts.note: a sexually transmitted disease
U denotes upper-class, as in U and non-U usage

explanation.surface: A posh philanderer catches a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a sexually active man, a womaniser.

clue.text: Jump jet regularly starts to nosedive during flip

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A vertical take-off aircraft begins to dive while it rolls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like a link word but its first letter is needed too, as the plural 'starts' covers two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, which is to flip it over.

clue.text: Unite enraged about partisan report's conclusions, say

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for angry surrounds the other letters

parts.note: irate means angry

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so the last letter of each of the two preceding words is taken

parts.note: final letter
final letter of report, the possessive tying it to conclusions
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring together people angered by a biased report's findings.
explanation.walkthrough: The angry word is split after its first letter to take the inserted pieces; 'say' is the usual crossword cue for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine separate parts into one whole, which is to unite them.

clue.text: Dishevelled robe on heavenly body

indicators.note: something dishevelled is untidy and out of place, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rumpled gown worn by some celestial figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon is also the fairy king in A Midsummer Night's Dream, which fits the robed surface figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the larger moons of Uranus, and a moon counts as a heavenly body.

clue.text: Troubled ex-Marine given drug test again

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
E is the street name for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A disturbed former soldier is drug-tested a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug's E joins the fodder before the shuffle; 'given' adds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means once more, so the word means to examine or test a second time.

clue.text: Fiendish new setter caught on tape?

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another sets it after, so the new setter caught follows the tape

parts.note: a demo tape is a band's sample recording
N is the abbreviation for new
the setter refers to themself as I
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A newcomer crossword compiler is fiendishly recorded on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'X on Y' puts X after Y, so N, I and C follow DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonic means like a demon, and a fiend is a demon, so fiendish fits.

clue.text: Home Counties captivated by aristocratic journalist's nasal outburst

indicators.note: someone captivated by another is held captive within them

parts.note: noble means aristocratic
the counties around London lie in south-east England
ED is an editor; the 's means 'journalist has'

explanation.surface: The posh newspaperman's snort reveals he is charmed by the commuter belt.
explanation.walkthrough: NO(SE)BLE + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebleed is a sudden flow of blood from the nose, jokily an outburst.

clue.text: English churchman taking turn in courtyard trembled

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the courtyard word

parts.note: a quad is a college quadrangle

indicators.note: taking a turn means rotating round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Rev is a reverend

explanation.surface: An English vicar strolling in a cloister was shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: A quad is the enclosed courtyard of a British college or school.
explanation.definitionFit: Quavered means shook or wavered, especially of a voice, which is to have trembled.

clue.text: Uniform covered in strong-smelling, phosphorus-free ointment

indicators.note: something covered in another thing is wrapped inside it
free of the element means its chemical symbol is removed

parts.note: a pungent smell is sharp and strong
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A uniform smeared with smelly but phosphorus-free cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong-smelling' first loses its chemical-symbol letter, then wraps around the NATO-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unguent is a formal word for a soothing salve or ointment rubbed on the skin.

clue.text: Follow story on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means broadcast and so heard, not read

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Keep up with a serial being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them covertly, which is to follow.

clue.text: Immature lout taken aback by silence on island

indicators.note: taken aback plays on being startled and on being turned back to front

parts.note: yob is British slang for a hooligan
I is the abbreviation for island
sh is the hushing sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: A childish thug is startled by a hush descending on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY from YOB backwards, then SH placed on I: BOY + I + SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means like a boy, youthful and not grown up, hence immature.

clue.text: Colonial hairstyle?

parts.note: surface reading: a hairdo from the colonies or the colonial era
setter's reading: colonial as in housing an insect colony, so a coiffure shaped like their home

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'colonial' is not about empire but about a colony of honey makers.
explanation.definitionFit: A beehive is a tall 1960s bouffant hairdo named for its resemblance to a hive.

clue.text: See 4
Damage from vehicle left one in confused state

indicators.note: in places the left-and-one pair inside the word for a muddled state

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a daze is a bewildered state
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Harm caused by a van abandoned by someone in a bewildered state.
explanation.walkthrough: VAN then DA(LI)ZE; the -IZE spelling is the setter's choice of the two accepted forms.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalize is to deliberately damage property, so damage works as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Assassin kept in isolation in jail

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A killer held in solitary confinement in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In isolation' suggests solitary confinement but the answer runs across isolatioN IN JAil.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese covert agent trained in stealthy killing, an assassin.

clue.text: Religious scholar cut short talk

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is chopped off the end

parts.note: rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for chatter

explanation.surface: A learned cleric's lecture was curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk' looks like a noun for the scholar's lecture; it is the verb rabbit, to chatter at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher learned in religious law, so a religious scholar.

clue.text: Controversy about contrary athlete

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A dispute over an awkward sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' looks like it describes the athlete, but it turns the short word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower competes in rowing, an Olympic sport, so is a kind of athlete.

clue.text: Organised group that chases criminals off

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it
the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A gang that hunts down crooks is put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' sits at the end as if part of the chase, but it is the definition, as in food gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is spoiled, and rancid describes stale, spoiled fat or butter.

clue.text: Burly, Welsh scoundrel becomes carnival attraction

parts.note: burly means big and strong
W is the abbreviation for Welsh
a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A hefty Welsh villain turns into a fairground draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' reads as part of a description of the scoundrel, but it supplies only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Big wheel is the British name for a Ferris wheel, a fixture of fairs and carnivals.

clue.text: Dull clergyman touring Dordogne on vacation

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the churchman goes around the other letters

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outside letters of the region

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boring vicar tours the Dordogne region of France on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as holidaying, but it says the region name is emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To deaden something is to make it dull, as with sound or pain.

clue.text: Humiliates German artist partaking in perverse deeds

indicators.note: partaking in means taking part inside, so the pair sits within the other letters
perverse means contrary or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A German painter who joins in twisted acts disgraces people.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; the rearranged deeds split around the German pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to lower their dignity, which is to humiliate them.
